I kick up taco night by subbing a radish coleslaw for the shredded lettuce and adding chorizo to the ground beef. They became way more popular than expected, and have come to be known simply as "Slawcos."

Make the slaw
Get this:
* green cabbage
* radishes
* mayo
* vinegar (rice, white, ACV)
* can corn
* salt, cayenne, cumin (optional)

Do this:

  1. Shred green cabbage and radishes in roughly equal portions.
  2. Add 6-10 Tsp mayo if you used the whole head of cabbage. The amount is really to taste, just add enough to give it an appropriate consistency.
  3. Add 2 Tsp rice or cider vinegar if you used the whole head of cabbage. 1 Tsp if using white vinegar.
  4. Add a can of corn and a pinch of salt and spices.
  5. Stick it in the fridge.

Start some rice
I recommend brown, but it's whatever.

Heat up a can of black beans
You should also take a short break and ponder life so the rice can get a good head start.

Meat
Cook a 50/50 mix of ground beef and chorizo in a skillet until no additional oil evolves from the sausage. I chop away at everything with a plastic spatula or wooden spoon for the entire time it cooks to get it all broken up and mixed. Now drain it. You won't be able to drain it like you can straight ground beef, so just give it your best.

Grub
Lay out the slaw, beans, rice, meat, and some shredded cheese with taco shells and/or tortillas. I'm normally a crunchy taco guy, but I think these are actually best on a soft flour tortilla.
